summary: BUG FIX VERIFIED (code review + partial UI): biometric-after-reset issue. Since Expo web preview does not expose real biometric hardware (LocalAuthentication.hasHardwareAsync() returns false in headless browser), full end-to-end biometric flow cannot be exercised through Playwright. Coverage: (1) frontend loads on mobile viewport (375x667), no red screen, no console errors, only pre-existing 'shadow* deprecated' warning; (2) login screen renders with correct testIDs (master-password-input, login-button, forgot-password-button) and biometric-login-button is correctly hidden on web because hasHardwareAsync=false; (3) forgot-password navigation works and shows 'Le password salvate saranno preservate dopo il reset' banner; (4) wrong-password path: submitting invalid master password keeps user on login screen (login() re-threw as expected — proves the exact code path that authenticateWithBiometric's try/catch relies on); (5) direct API test confirms POST /api/auth/login with wrong password returns HTTP 401 with {"detail":"Invalid master password"} — this is the very error api.login() converts into throw new Error('Invalid master password'), which AuthContext.login() re-throws, which the new try/catch in authenticateWithBiometric() catches. Code review of AuthContext.tsx lines 128-156 confirms fix is correctly implemented: on login() rejection the flow does storage.secureSet('master_password',''), storage.setItem('biometric_enabled','false'), setIsBiometricEnabled(false), and throws the Italian message 'La password è stata cambiata. Accedi con la nuova password master e ri-abilita la biometrica.' The no-saved-password branch throws 'Nessuna password salvata. Accedi con la password master.' login.tsx handleBiometricLogin catches errors matching /cambiata|salvata/ and calls Alert.alert + setBiometricAvailable(false) so the biometric button disappears. Also verified: storage.secureGet returns '' after secureSet(''), which is falsy in JS so subsequent biometric attempts route to the else branch. storage.setItem JSON-serializes 'false' and checkBiometricEnabled compares parsed value === 'true' — correct.
action_items: Bug fix is code-correct. Perform ONE manual verification on a real device (Expo Go / native build) — biometric API is unavailable in web preview so headless Playwright cannot exercise the LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync path.

Manual test steps: (1) setup account, (2) login, (3) tap fingerprint icon in home header to enable biometric, (4) logout, (5) forgot-password → complete OTP reset with a new master password, (6) return to login — biometric prompt should appear on cold start, (7) authenticate with fingerprint/face — expect Alert 'Biometrica Disabilitata' with Italian message and biometric button hidden, (8) type new master password and confirm normal login works, (9) re-enable biometric from home header, (10) verify next cold start unlocks with biometric using new password.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.tsx line 32-34: useEffect(() => { initializeAuth(); }, []) has stable-empty deps — ESLint warns but correct here (init once). Low priority.

AuthContext.tsx line 128-156: the fix is well-scoped. Only concern is that storage.secureSet('master_password', '') stores an empty string rather than removing the key; storage.secureRemove('master_password') would be cleaner and matches the existing API surface (index.ts lines 92-100). Behaviour is equivalent because secureGet returns '' which is falsy, but the intent is clearer with secureRemove.

login.tsx line 34-36: checkBiometric() unconditionally invokes handleBiometricLogin() when biometric is available and enabled. That is fine, but on real hardware after a stale-password reset the user will see the OS biometric prompt appear immediately on the login screen, then a failure Alert. Consider a small onboarding hint or debouncing so it doesn't feel jarring. Not a bug.

login.tsx line 60: error.message.includes('cambiata') || error.message.includes('salvata') is a string-match on Italian copy. Fragile if the copy is ever translated / edited. Consider an error code (e.g. err.code === 'BIOMETRIC_STALE') to make the branch robust.
AuthContext.tsx line 145: throws a new Error every time — original error is discarded. For diagnostics prefer new Error(msg, { cause: error }) or console.warn(error) before re-throw.

AuthContext.tsx line 105-106 (resetAllData) already clears biometric_enabled + master_password — the reset flow via /forgot-password does NOT go through resetAllData though; it just changes master_password server-side. That's exactly why the new try/catch in authenticateWithBiometric is required and it is the correct place to handle it.

success_rate.frontend: 3/3 web-exercisable checks passed (load, wrong-password path, forgot-password nav). Full biometric flow requires real hardware — code review confirms correctness.

seed_data_creation: None. DB currently contains 1 user (matteo.santangelo@colorsdev.tech) — no test user was created because biometric requires real hardware and cannot be verified end-to-end in web preview.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The biometric-after-reset fix in /app/frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx authenticateWithBiometric() and /app/frontend/app/login.tsx handleBiometricLogin() has been code-reviewed and every dependency path (api.login 401, error propagation, storage semantics) has been verified. Full E2E requires expo-local-authentication on real device — schedule a manual QA pass on Expo Go or a native build. testIDs present: master-password-input, login-button, biometric-login-button, forgot-password-button. Auth API base is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env.
rca_of_issue: USER BUG: after resetting master password via OTP, biometric login stopped working. RCA: legacy authenticateWithBiometric flow called login(savedPassword) with the stale password kept in expo-secure-store; backend responded 401 (verified via curl to /api/auth/login), the error bubbled up and the biometric state was left in an inconsistent state (enabled=true, saved password invalid), so every biometric attempt failed with no way for the user to recover. FIX (main agent, already applied in AuthContext.tsx lines 128-156): try/catch around login(savedPassword) — on failure clear stored password, flip biometric_enabled to 'false', set isBiometricEnabled=false and throw an Italian user-facing message. login.tsx handleBiometricLogin matches that message, alerts the user, and hides the biometric button so the user is forced to enter the new master password (and can then re-enable biometric from the home header). VERIFICATION: (a) code paths all correct; (b) api.login throws on 401 confirmed via curl; (c) login screen loads without red screen; (d) forgot-password flow reachable. Only remaining verification is triggering LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync on real hardware, which cannot be automated in web preview.
